recipes.title: Moroccan chickpea & apricot tagine
recipes.summary: A fragrant tomato, chickpea and apricot stew with couscous and lemon.
ingredients: A handful of parsley or coriander
steps: Soften the onion in 1 tbsp olive oil for 6–8 minutes. Add the garlic and spices; stir for 1 minute.
Add pepper and courgette. Cook 5 minutes, then add tomatoes, chickpeas, apricots and stock.
Simmer uncovered for 20–25 minutes, until the vegetables are soft and the sauce is thick. Season with salt, pepper and lemon juice.
Prepare couscous according to the packet. Fluff with a fork and a little olive oil. Serve the tagine over it with herbs and extra lemon.
recipes.note: Use two tins of chickpeas for a more substantial main meal; The method can be refined based on further cooking feedback. Cooked at least twice, confirmed 14 October 2026; exact dates not recorded.

nutrition.basis: Qualitative ingredient-based indication, not a nutrient calculation or adequacy rating.
nutrition.note: Protein improves with an added soy food or extra legumes. Standard couscous is usually refined, not whole grain. Chickpea tin drained weights and added oil change nutrition substantially.

recipes.title: Miso-ginger roasted tofu & vegetables
recipes.summary: Sweet potato, crisp tofu and vegetables in a savoury miso glaze.
ingredients: 300 g firm tofu, pressed and cubed
150–200 g fresh green beans, optional; if frozen, thaw and drain separately
steps: Start the rice according to the packet. Heat the oven to 210°C fan. Toss the sweet potato in a little oil and roast for 15 minutes.
Dry the tofu well. Brown it in a pan with a little oil until its edges are firm and golden.

Mix miso, soy sauce, vinegar, sesame oil, ginger, sweetener and 1–2 tbsp water. Add broccoli and pepper to the tray; roast another 12–15 minutes. Cook fresh beans separately until tender, or thaw/cook and drain frozen beans thoroughly.
Toss the hot roasted vegetables and tofu with the glaze; fold in drained green beans near the end. Serve with rice, spring onions and sesame.
recipes.note: You tried frozen green beans in the roast. They released water and made the tray too juicy. Use fresh broccoli/beans, or thaw and drain frozen beans and cook them separately before combining.

nutrition.basis: Qualitative ingredient-based indication, not a nutrient calculation or adequacy rating.

macro.Fat: Cooking oil, sesame oil and sesame seeds
macro.Fibre: Broccoli, green beans and sweet potato

micro.sources: Tofu if calcium-set; broccoli also contributes

nutrition.note: Calcium varies greatly with tofu brand and coagulant; check the label. Soy sauce and miso contribute sodium. Rice variety influences fibre and minerals.

recipes.title: Korean-style tofu bowl
recipes.summary: Crisp tofu, rice, crunchy vegetables and a tangy soy-chilli dressing.
ingredients: 300 g firm tofu, pressed and cubed
steps: Cook the rice according to the packet.
Pat tofu dry and pan-fry in a little oil until thoroughly browned on all sides.
Whisk soy sauce, vinegar, sesame oil, maple syrup and gochujang. Toss half with the tofu.
Divide rice and vegetables between bowls, add tofu, and finish with the rest of the dressing, spring onion and sesame.
recipes.note: You rated the bowl “very nice.” The recipe here is a practical reconstruction of the dish, so adjust the dressing to match the version you liked.

nutrition.basis: Qualitative ingredient-based indication, not a nutrient calculation or adequacy rating.

macro.Fat: Sesame oil, seeds and cooking oil
macro.Fibre: Vegetables; more if spinach rather than cucumber-heavy

micro.sources: Cabbage and vegetables (amount depends on selection)

nutrition.note: A higher tofu-to-rice ratio increases protein density. Spinach contributes folate and vitamin K but its calcium is poorly absorbed. Soy sauce raises sodium.

recipes.title: Vietnamese glass-noodle & tempeh salad
recipes.summary: A cool, crunchy salad that comes together when the dressing hits the raw vegetables.
ingredients: 100 g dry glass noodles (50 g per portion)
A handful of fresh mint or coriander
30 g roasted peanuts or chilli nuts
steps: Prepare the noodles according to the packet, rinse cool and drain well.
Slice and pan-fry the tempeh until browned; splash with a little soy sauce.
Whisk lime, vinegar, soy sauce, sweetener, garlic and optional chilli.
Toss noodles, raw vegetables and herbs with the dressing. Top with warm tempeh and nuts.
recipes.note: The raw vegetables worked well once dressed. Your successful amounts were 50 g dry noodles and 100 g tempeh per portion; chilli nuts were a good substitute.

nutrition.basis: Qualitative ingredient-based indication, not a nutrient calculation or adequacy rating.

macro.Carbohydrate: Glass noodles and a little dressing sugar
macro.Fibre: Raw vegetables, tempeh and peanuts; glass noodles add little

nutrition.note: Glass noodles are largely starch; tempeh and peanuts carry most of the protein, fibre and minerals. Tempeh is not a reliable vitamin B12 source.

recipes.title: Smoky Mexican black-bean fajita bowls
recipes.summary: Charred peppers, beans, sweetcorn, avocado and lime. Add tofu for more protein.
ingredients: 2 peppers, cut into small taco-friendly pieces
2 tins black beans (about 480 g each), drained
Fresh coriander, olive oil, salt and pepper
steps: Cook the rice. Brown the tofu separately if using.
Cook peppers and onion in a hot pan with oil until softened with charred edges. Add cumin and smoked paprika.
Warm both tins of black beans and sweetcorn with the vegetables. Add fresh chopped tomatoes only near the end.
Serve in crispy taco shells or over rice with tofu, avocado and coriander. Squeeze lime over everything only just before serving.
recipes.note: Approved. Use two 480 g tins of black beans for two peppers, cut peppers into small taco-friendly pieces, add tomatoes late and lime only at the end. Crispy taco shells work well.

nutrition.basis: Qualitative ingredient-based indication, not a nutrient calculation or adequacy rating.

macro.Protein: Black beans; more if optional tofu included

nutrition.note: Tofu is optional, so protein and calcium vary. Two large tins of beans add substantial fibre; drained tin weights need checking. Lime and peppers supply vitamin C alongside plant iron.

recipes.title: Ethiopian berbere red lentils
recipes.summary: A warming spiced lentil stew with a slow-cooked onion base.
ingredients: About 700 ml water or vegetable stock, added as needed
steps: Cook the onion gently in oil for 20–30 minutes until very soft and golden.
Add garlic, ginger and berbere; stir for a minute. Add lentils and most of the liquid.
Simmer gently, stirring and adding liquid as needed. Allow 40–50 minutes or until the lentils are fully tender.
Add the tomatoes once the lentils have begun to soften, then simmer to a rich, thick consistency. Season with salt and lemon; serve with rice or flatbread.
recipes.note: Your onions needed much longer and the lentils took more than 40 minutes. The 700 ml liquid and delayed tomato are practical refinements; judge by tenderness.

nutrition.basis: Qualitative ingredient-based indication, not a nutrient calculation or adequacy rating.

macro.Carbohydrate: Red lentils plus optional rice or bread

nutrition.note: Rice or flatbread is optional and changes the energy and carbohydrate content. Lentils are a valuable protein/fibre base, but this meal provides little B12, D or long-chain omega-3.

recipes.title: Italian white-bean, mushroom & cavolo-nero stew
recipes.summary: Earthy mushrooms and beans with a generous helping of greens.
ingredients: 2 tins white beans (400 g each), drained
150–200 g cavolo nero, stems removed and leaves finely chopped
Lemon juice or a splash of vinegar
steps: Soften onion in olive oil for 8 minutes. Add mushrooms and cook until their water evaporates and they brown.
Add garlic and herbs for 1 minute, then tomatoes, beans and stock. Simmer 15 minutes.
Add finely chopped cavolo nero and cook until tender, allowing 10–15 minutes or longer for tougher leaves.
Season and add lemon or vinegar just before serving.
recipes.note: The cavolo nero needed longer than expected; chop it more finely or add it earlier.

nutrition.basis: Qualitative ingredient-based indication, not a nutrient calculation or adequacy rating.

macro.Fibre: White beans, cavolo nero and mushrooms

nutrition.note: Mushrooms do not reliably supply vitamin D unless UV-treated. Cook the cavolo nero long enough to soften; vitamin C is sensitive to prolonged heating.

recipes.title: Thai red tofu, aubergine & green-bean curry
recipes.summary: Coconut red curry with black rice and a whole lime for a lively finish.
ingredients: 200 g green beans, fresh or frozen
2–3 tbsp Thai red curry paste (check it is vegan if needed)
steps: Start black rice according to your packet; yours takes about 50 minutes.
Brown tofu thoroughly in a pan and set aside. Fry aubergine until softened and golden.
Stir in curry paste for a minute, then coconut milk and water. Simmer aubergine for about 10 minutes.
Add green beans and simmer until truly tender; frozen beans need longer. Return tofu to warm through.
Finish with zest and juice of the whole lime, then serve over black rice.
recipes.note: Approved as “nice.” Longer tofu browning, extra cooking for frozen beans and the full lime made this version work.

nutrition.basis: Qualitative ingredient-based indication, not a nutrient calculation or adequacy rating.

macro.Fibre: Aubergine, green beans and black rice

nutrition.note: Coconut milk makes this relatively rich in saturated fat. The amount and brand matter. Consider lighter coconut milk when you want a lower-saturated-fat version; paste can also be salty.

recipes.title: Italian chicken & vegetable traybake
recipes.summary: A simple oven supper of chicken, potatoes, peppers, tomatoes and green beans.
steps: Heat oven to 200°C fan. Toss potatoes, peppers and onion with oil, herbs, salt and pepper. Roast 20 minutes.
Season the chicken separately. Add chicken, green beans and cherry tomatoes to the tray; scatter chorizo if using.
Roast another 15–20 minutes, turning as needed, until the chicken is cooked through (74°C in the thickest part) and potatoes are tender. Rest chicken briefly.
recipes.note: The earlier traybake looked tasty. Adding the chicken after the vegetables helps keep the fillets juicy.

nutrition.basis: Qualitative ingredient-based indication, not a nutrient calculation or adequacy rating.

macro.Fat: Olive oil; optional chorizo adds fat

nutrition.note: Chorizo is optional, adding saturated fat and salt; omit for the leaner version. Fibre may be lower than in bean-based recipes.

recipes.title: Spanish chicken, white-bean & pepper traybake
recipes.summary: Smoky paprika chicken and roasted peppers with creamy white beans.
steps: Heat oven to 200°C fan. Toss peppers, onion and tomatoes with olive oil, garlic, half the paprika, oregano and seasoning. Roast 20 minutes.
Rub chicken separately with remaining paprika, oil, herbs, salt and pepper. Stir beans into the vegetables, then nestle chicken on top.
Roast another 15–20 minutes, depending on thickness, until chicken reaches 74°C in its centre. Rest a few minutes and finish with lemon.
recipes.note: You liked this as “a nice change,” but chicken overcooked when it went in with the vegetables. Stagger the roasting as above.

nutrition.basis: Qualitative ingredient-based indication, not a nutrient calculation or adequacy rating.
nutrition.note: A useful combination of animal protein and legumes. Add the chicken partway through roasting to prevent drying out. No firm calcium or vitamin D source.

recipes.title: Persian-style chicken with fruit & rice
recipes.summary: Fragrant spice, tart fruit and herbs over rice.
ingredients: 60 g dried barberries, or dried cranberries
30 g chopped pistachios or almonds, optional
steps: Cook rice according to the packet. If using barberries, rinse briefly; if using cranberries, add extra lemon for tartness.
Soften onion in oil, then add turmeric and cinnamon. Add chicken and cook, turning, until browned and cooked through (74°C).
Warm the fruit briefly with a spoon of water and a little lemon juice; avoid burning it.
Serve chicken and fruit over rice with parsley, nuts and more lemon to taste.
recipes.note: You used cranberries because barberries are difficult to find in Sweden. The result was good but lacked their tartness; add lemon to taste. Quantities are reconstructed, not a record of precisely what you used. Later feedback: increase the fruit sauce with stock and a little extra liquid to avoid dryness; bloom saffron in a spoon of warm water and add to sauce or rice.

nutrition.basis: Qualitative ingredient-based indication, not a nutrient calculation or adequacy rating.

macro.Fat: Olive oil and optional pistachios or almonds
macro.Fibre: Onion, nuts and dried fruit; relatively little without a side vegetable

nutrition.note: Serve with a generous green vegetable or salad for fibre, folate and vitamin C. Dried cranberries are often sweetened; barberries differ. Add stock to keep the sauce juicy.

recipes.title: Greek butter beans with spinach, tofu, olives & feta
recipes.summary: Creamy butter beans in a juicy tomato sauce with golden tofu, spinach, Kalamata olives, feta and lemon.
ingredients: 2 tins butter beans (about 400 g each), drained
150 ml vegetable stock, plus extra if needed
Black pepper; salt only after tasting
steps: Pat the tofu dry, cube it and fry in a little olive oil until golden on several sides (about 8 minutes). Set aside.
Soften onion in the same pan for 4–5 minutes. Add garlic, oregano and smoked paprika for 30 seconds, then tomato purée for another minute.
Add tomatoes, drained butter beans and stock. Simmer uncovered for 15 minutes, stirring occasionally. Keep the sauce generous and juicy.
Add spinach until wilted. Fold in tofu and olives and simmer gently for about 3–5 minutes.
Turn off heat, add juice of half a lemon and chopped parsley. Taste before adding salt, as the olives and feta are salty. Scatter crumbled feta over just before serving.
recipes.note: You described the dish as very nice. Kalamata olives and feta are the preferred additions. Keep extra stock handy for leftovers. With dairy feta this is vegetarian; omit or replace with plant-based feta for vegan.

nutrition.basis: Qualitative ingredient-based indication, not a nutrient calculation or adequacy rating.

macro.Protein: Butter beans and tofu; feta adds some

micro.sources: Feta and calcium-set tofu; spinach calcium is poorly absorbed
Feta contributes some, not a guaranteed daily supply

nutrition.note: Olives and feta increase sodium; season after tasting. Calcium depends strongly on the tofu brand. Spinach is not a reliable high-absorption calcium source.
